title: Vaim by Jon Fosse
text:
Vaim by Jon Fosse
Vaim
by Jon Fosse
translated by Damion Searls
Transit Books, 2025, 135 pages, US$25.95
Jon Fosse is the fourth Norwegian to be awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature, but he’s the first one writing in Nynorsk to receive it. Nynorsk is a form of Norwegian developed in the nineteenth century to create a language based on the myriad of Norwegian dialects, but without the Danish influence that so pervades them all. (There’s an old joke that goes: every Norwegian speaks four languages—three of which are Norwegian.) The Nobel committee’s citation said they were bestowing the award “for his innovative plays and prose which give voice to the unsayable”. Throughout his latest book, Vaim, we get the characters’ stream of consciousness where their thoughts go right up to the point of what they want to say but cannot.
